## Data Source:
The full El-Nino/La-Nina data can be found [here](https://ourworldindata.org/global-temperatures-el-nino-la-nina).

## Using the Data Package

The first thing to do is to load the library.

```{r setup,eval=FALSE}
library(SquareR)
```
This will enable the use of the data, called el_nino. Next, load and assign the data to a data frame.
```{r}
data <- as.data.frame(SquareR::el_nino)
```
Next, we can simply plot the data with R's default functions, like so, adding a day value to "Months," and changing the vector to be a date:
```{r}
#This is needed to be recognized as a date.
data$Month <- paste0(data$Month, "-01") 
data$Month <- as.Date(data$Month)
```
Note that 'theme' creates colours in-between the chosen values (here light blue and firebrick), then calling it using a number tells the function hw many colours to use (it will repeat when reaching the end of the colours).
```{r, fig.align='center'}
theme <- colorRampPalette(c("lightblue", "firebrick2"))

plot(data$Month, data$`Temperature anomaly`, 
  xlab = "Year", 
  ylab = "Temperature Anomaly", 
  main = "Global El-Nino/La-Nina Effect\n Versus the 1990-2020 Average Temperature",
  pch = 21, #symbol shape
  cex = 0.75, #symbol size
  bg = theme(920)) #background colour. "col =" returns outline colour.
```
